A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same residual-decomposition conformal prediction framework, despite the changed title and formatting. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments and automobile and stock forecasting results in Section 7 and Appendix D, including coverage, interval widths, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic and real-world experiments and adds baseline comparisons, parameter sweeps, and single-stage controls in Section 8 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the adaptive update from alpha_t + gamma(alpha − cov_t) to alpha_t + gamma(alpha − (1 − cov_t)). This aligns the pseudocode with the update already used in v1's proof; it does not establish an implementation change. The residual decomposition, interval constructions, FWER selection, and other adaptive components remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate linear and nonlinear synthetic pipelines, stationary mixing data, upstream/downstream and covariate shifts, automobile indicators, and the same stock forecasting task. V2's single-stage controls and parameter sweeps change model configurations and evaluation procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Cascaded Confidence, specifically its K-means variant, to non-adaptive comparisons in Tables 3–6 and Figures 5–6. ECI joins synthetic, automobile, and stock comparisons; it was cited but not evaluated in v1. Appendix D.4.8 also adds direct single-stage least-squares, VAR, and ARIMA controls. DtACI was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds multi-alpha coverage–width evaluations, comparisons of tolerance 0 versus 0.05 across retained shifts, an automobile summary over the last 50 months, and single-stage predictive controls. Reported settings also change: the signed-heuristic table's alpha changes from 0.01 to 0.10, and the automobile appendix caption changes delta from 0.3 to 0.1. The latter conflicts with v2's main caption, so it does not establish a consistent experimental rerun.

E4.justification: New single-stage controls in Appendix D.4.8 test whether gains arise from better predictors or from exploiting residual decomposition. Figures 2, 5, 6, and 13 expand analysis of calibration, width, and tolerance across nominal coverage levels. Existing quantile-update, targeted-retraining, covariate-shift, and other hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Retained tables preserve their stated 50-run/sample counts and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. New plots continue the standard-deviation convention. No changed repetition counts, seed practices, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial CC, ECI, single-stage, and coverage–width results. Reported automobile mean widths change from 21.085 to 18.957 for SR and from 31.058 to 15.667 for OCID, alongside revised trajectories and findings. These are changed reported results, not established same-setting improvements. Many earlier tabulated values remain, including the original entries of v1 Table 1, now v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: V1 Proposition 2 becomes Proposition 5.5 with component quantiles at 1 − alpha/2, correcting the existence proof's unsupported inference from a 1 − 2alpha endpoint to 1 − alpha coverage. The Hoeffding exponent is also revised. V2 removes v1 Proposition 6 and Lemma A.3 concerning finite-sample hidden-Markov bounds, while retaining the long-run guarantee and mixing extension.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion qualify the empirical claim: v1 says coverage is maintained under shifts, whereas v2 emphasizes improved relative coverage and less severe degradation under structural, stage-wise shifts. The central decomposition, FWER calibration, adaptive extension, and long-run coverage contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds the interpretation that improved forecasting alone cannot explain the coverage gains, drawing on single-stage controls. It discusses circumstances where tolerance 0.05 loses to WSC under rapid upstream shifts, and interprets CC's wide intervals and ECI's tight intervals as contrasting calibration failures. The automobile discussion also changes from OCID covering the shock with wide intervals to attributing its partial coverage to unstable widths.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's hardware and baseline hyperparameters, v2 adds a code-repository link and Appendix D.2's candidate-grid specification, granularity guidance, initialization choices, and parameter-selection workflow. It also documents ECI's step size and the new VAR(3) and ARIMA(2,0,1) controls. These materially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to previously undisclosed settings.

R1.justification: A dedicated Related Work section substantially expands positioning beyond v1's brief overview. It introduces medical-imaging uncertainty-propagation work and identifies Gong et al.'s cascaded-module method as the closest comparison, distinguishing its decomposition from the proposed FWER and adaptive approach. Foundational and survey citations are added, and several older references are removed.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, author/venue material, terminology, and numerous explanatory sentences. It introduces a Related Work section, revises the non-adaptive experimental narrative, and reorganizes Appendix D around guidance and comparisons. Most existing method exposition, proof text, and the overall methodological sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, relocates the original main results table to Appendix Table 3 with a CC column, and foregrounds coverage–width plots. It adds multi-panel baseline and single-stage figures, expands existing plots with ECI, and changes legends, captions, sizing, and figure placement throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects an important gap in the scaling-existence argument and the inconsistent adaptive pseudocode. The previously missing close CC comparison and new single-stage controls materially strengthen evaluation and research positioning, while grid guidance and code-access information improve reproducibility. Removing the hidden-Markov finite-sample bound narrows theoretical scope, and some revised results retain inconsistent setting labels. Nevertheless, the gains in mathematical consistency and empirical scrutiny provide substantial overall improvement.
